newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Dollar/yen vols ebb as spot calms.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/yen vols ebb as spot calms.

text.p: Implied volatilities on dollar/yen options fell across the board in Europe as activity in spot dollar/yen calmed after Monday's drop to an almost four-month low.
One-month dollar/yen vols dropped to 10.20/10.60 percent by 1045 GMT from 11.00/11.50 in late European trade on Monday. One-year vols were at 9.20/9.50 against 9.70/10.00.
Volatilities shot up across the curve yesterday following a slide of about six yen in spot dollar/yen since late last week, but vols were ebbing now that spot was steadying at around 119 yen.

"There are people who are looking to sell dollar puts if we see spot levels well above 119 yen, but the risk reversal in dollar/yen still seems to be well bid for dollar puts," said Satu Jaatinen, options trader at Chase Manhattan Bank here.
One-month 25-delta risk reversal for dollar/yen was at 0.8/1.2 in favour of dollar puts against 1.1/1.6 on Monday.

Mark/yen vols softened as the spot rate recovered from its lowest in nearly a year, hit on Monday, and broke back above 70 yen. One-month mark/yen vols were at 9.00/9.40 percent against 9.60/9.90. Demand for mark puts did not ease, however, with one-month risk reversal unchanged at 0.5/0.9 in favour of mark puts.
Dollar/mark was sidelined, with one-month vols remaining steady at 8.85/9.15 percent against late Monday's 8.75/9.00.

"We've seen quite a few sellers of dollar puts in periods of one and two months, and buyers of dollar calls in long dates. So generally the picture for dollar/mark is a much more confident one than for dollar/yen," Chase's Jaatinen said.
One-month dollar/mark risk reversal, favouring mark calls, eased to 0.0/0.3 from 0.3/0.7.

Sterling/mark volatilities were softer across the curve. Spot sterling/mark was buoyed by the Bank of England's inflation report today which called for a fresh rise in interest rates and warned inflation was likely to overshoot without more policy action.
One-month sterling/mark vols were at 9.30/9.60 percent against Monday's 9.60/10.10, and 7.90/8.20 against 8.00/8.50 for one-year options.
